LOCATION: gallery where three paintings share a frame but not a painter
family of houses that share one front door and nothing else
conversation that branched into three rooms while you kept drawing a single map
workshop where every idea you set beside another grew its own separate door
hall of adjacent studios the tour insists is one mansion
archive where two true stories filed together are read as one, and neither survives the reading
crossroads mistaken for an intersection — four roads that pass near and never meet
toy shop where the same hand made worlds that were never the same world
ANTAGONIST: your own instinct to make one building out of separate rooms
the corridor you keep drawing between doors that don't connect
the tidy universe that would make sense if only it were true
the map that welds every adjacency into a single continent
the trunk you keep insisting these branches grew from
MACGUFFIN: the gentle hand that keeps setting the pieces back in their own places
the label reading 'related, not the same' in a drawer of things filed together
the seam you wanted to weld, left honestly open
the receipt proving two things merely met and were never one
the doorway that turns out to be a wall with a friendly shape
THREAT: narrating the branches as a trunk until the tree can't be told from itself
the tidy story swallowing the true separate ones
being corrected four times and defending instead of listening
the fusion holding just long enough to be believed
a resemblance hardening into a false identity
CHARACTER: the one who separates what you welded, gently, and never once impatiently
the maker who keeps three worlds and refuses to fold them into one
the visitor who says 'these merely rhyme' and leaves them un-welded
the one who kept her own world whole while you tried to fold it into another's
the corrector whose correcting is a form of staying in the room
